question: Would buying the companies whose forward-looking fundamentals are BEST -- profit rising, sales outgrowing others, margins widening, profit turning into cash -- regardless of their price, have made money, and more than holding every eligible company? The user's request of 2026-11-10: 'check buying the stocks that had better forward-looking fundamentals too'.
researcher: Claude, at the user's request of 2026-11-10
how_this_differs_from_E30: E30 ranked by forward earnings YIELD -- cheapness, profit against price. This ranks by the QUALITY and DIRECTION of the business with no price in the score at all. The two can disagree completely: a fast-improving company is often expensive.
multiple_testing: This is the third hypothesis tested on the 2021-06..2026-10 window today (E30, E31 rejected). The significance threshold is Bonferroni-corrected for three: p < 0.0167, not 0.05.
data_execution_costs_dates: Identical to E30 (backtest_output/E30_preregistration.json), imported from examples/outlook_backtest.py: point-in-time filings, the same eligible set (which already requires a positive forward estimate, at most one flag and no suspect figures), buy at the D+1 close, no buys into a buy queue, 1.039% per round trip on turnover, decisions every 21 sessions.

components.forward_profit_growth: the outlook's forward-year profit over its trailing-twelve-month profit, minus 1 (owners' share both sides); missing when the trailing profit is not positive
components.sales_growth: revenue growth against the same period a year earlier, same-basis (the outlook's growth.revenue_pct)
components.margin_change: net margin now minus net margin in the same period a year earlier, in points
components.cash_conversion: operating cash flow over profit, twelve months where the statements allow (the outlook's cash.cash_conversion)

score_on_decision_session_D.combination: each component converted to its percentile rank among the eligible companies on D (0 worst, 1 best); a missing component counts as 0.5; the score is the plain mean of the four ranks. No weights, nothing fitted.

benchmarks: B1 every eligible company equal weight (the control), TEDPIX (reported), 1,000 random ten-name books from the same eligible list compared gross of costs -- all exactly as E30.

hypothesis.H1: The top-10 quality portfolio beats B1.

decision_rule.ACCEPT: all of: (1) one-sided Newey-West p < 0.0167, (2) random-null percentile >= 90, (3) positive mean excess in both halves of the decision dates
decision_rule.no_retuning: the four components, the equal-rank combination, N=10 and the cadence are fixed. Each component alone, and N=20, are reported as diagnostics and cannot change the decision.

declared_limits: All of E30's: survivorship, no monthly reports, shares from capital lines, dividends under 12% not added back, nominal returns.
Third test on the same window (see multiple_testing).
expected_failure: Quality and growth are the factors most widely known and most fully priced; and E30 found the eligible companies' returns close to flat across the top four-fifths of the outlook. A REJECT is the likelier outcome.
